_readme: A1'S OWN ECONOMIC AND RATE INPUTS, read 2026-08-30 off their free
'EdgeFinder - Free Economic Data' report by driving its filters and reading
the rendered charts' own accessible data tables and tooltips.
WHY THIS FIXTURE IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER ONE HERE. The others record
A1's OUTPUT -- cells off a scorecard. This records their INPUT: the actual
and forecast numbers a cell is computed from. That turns 'our cell differs
from theirs' into an answerable question, because the two models can now be
compared at the point where they take their data in rather than at the point
IT IS EVIDENCE, NOT A FEED. Looker Studio embeds over A1's proprietary
'EdgeFinder Pro' data, no documented API. Nothing in this repo fetches them

source.method: Per page: set the currency/country control, then read the chart's own <table> data representation and, where a chart publishes no table, its hover tooltips. No value here was estimated from pixel geometry.
source.attribution: Every chart footers 'Source: A1 EdgeFinder Pro | www.a1trading.com'.

freeSurfaceMap._note: The complete page list of this report, read off its own navigation tree.
freeSurfaceMap._whatIsExposed: Most pages publish ACTUAL and FORECAST per country with real release dates and a date-range control, back to 2024 -- so they are historical AND date-addressable. Three exceptions matter: Unemployment Rate publishes the ACTUAL only (its second chart reads 'COMING SOON!' over a dataset error), Interest Rate Projections publishes no history at all, and no page carries currency-index rows.

dataUpdatesLog._note: A1's own list of their internal datasets and refresh cadences, read off the Data Updates Log page. It names the datasets, which is a map of their pipeline.
_twoFindings: There is NO 'interest rate projections' dataset in the log. The rate-side datasets are 'Central bank interest rates' (daily) and a 'Carry trade scanner' that appears nowhere else in the free surface.
'Retail sentiment' refreshes every 30 minutes, which explains why the snapshot page and the daily history page disagree on the same day -- they are the live feed and its daily roll-up.

scoringRulesInA1sOwnWords.gdp: GDP growth scores are based on a per-currency basis. If there is a beat in the forecasted GDP, it will be bullish for that currency and their respective indices. So, higher-than-expected GDP in the US would be a +1 for both USD and the indices. It is also a positive score for metals and commodities such as Silver, Copper, Platinum and USOil. Gold is the exception. A miss in GDP growth expectations will result in a negative score for the currency and its respective indices and commodities. Meanwhile, gold will get a positive score in that category.
scoringRulesInA1sOwnWords.pmi: A positive change in PMI suggests growth, or slower decline. So, if PMI in either category come in higher, it is considered optimistic for its currency (+1). However, this would impact other assets such as gold, in a negative way.
scoringRulesInA1sOwnWords.unemployment: The unemployment rate is the number of actively searching unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the labor force. A higher percentage usually causes weakness in the dollar and US indices.
scoringRulesInA1sOwnWords._silverContradictsTheirOwnText: Their GDP text says silver, copper, platinum and USOil score WITH the currency and only gold inverts. Their own cells disagree: on 2026-08-24 XAUUSD and XAGUSD carry identical gdp (+1), mpmi (-1) and consumer-confidence (+1) cells, which only works if silver inverts too. This repo follows their DATA (GOLD_POLARITY on both) and not their prose. Do not 'fix' it to match the text.

ppiClassificationIsThreeState._note: The PPI YoY chart labels each release Met / Lower than expected / Higher than expected as separate series. That is A1's comparison made visible: three states with no tolerance band, an exact match being its own category.
ppiClassificationIsThreeState.example: GBP 2025-08 printed 4.00% against a 4.00% forecast and lands in the 'Met' series, not in either tail.
ppiClassificationIsThreeState.consequence: It corroborates this repo's `scoreTernary`, which is a raw sign of (actual - forecast) with only a float-noise epsilon. An earlier +/-0.25 sigma deadband was removed for the same reason and must not come back.

series._note: actual/forecast pairs as A1 publishes them, most recent release first where several are recorded. `date` is A1's own release date.

unemploymentRateActualOnly._note: This page publishes no forecast, so it cannot settle the comparison basis for the unemployment column.

rateInputs._note: The two halves of A1's Interest Rates comparison, from two of their free pages on the same day.

projectionsFromProjectionsPage._precision: Tooltips round to one decimal, so USD 3.8 is the 3.75 the Interest Rates page carries and EUR 2.7 is 2.65.

derivedLegs._rule: cell = sign(current quarter's projected rate - standing policy rate), flat band 0.10pp
_reproduces: EURUSD +1 = EUR(+1) - USD(0)      2026-08-24 Top Setups, checksummed
GBPUSD +1 = GBP(+1) - USD(0)      2026-08-24 Top Setups, checksummed
EURCHF +1 = EUR(+1) - CHF(0)      2026-08-24 Top Setups, checksummed
EURCHF Bullish = EUR(+1) - CHF(0) 2026-08-29 free Forex Scorecard
derivedLegs._theOneException: EURX's 2026-08-24 rates cell reads 0 where this rule says +1. It is one cell from a crowded multi-row crop, and the projections chart has no history, so a revision between 08-24 and 08-30 cannot be ruled out either.
derivedLegs._rivalAssignmentRejected: Taking EURX at face value gives EUR 0, USD -1, GBP 0, CHF -1, which satisfies the same three pair equations. It matches A1's own published rate inputs for NOT ONE of those four currencies and needs CHF -1 while A1's pages put the Swiss policy rate and every projected quarter at 0.00%.
derivedLegs._whyItIsNOTIMPLEMENTED: Implemented, measured and reverted on 2026-08-30. The Fed is the only bank whose projection this repo holds, so adopting the rule moves USD's leg alone while EUR and GBP stay at a placeholder 0. Cell parity went 84/98 -> 82/98 and the rates column 5/6 -> 3/6 exact, with no cell gained. A1's rates column is a DIFFERENCE: it cannot be adopted one currency at a time.

rateInputs._ecbRateChoiceDiffers: A1's Interest Rates page carries EUR at 2.40%; this repo reads the ECB deposit facility and gets 2.25%. Their series steps 2.15 -> 2.40, which is the shape of the Main Refinancing Operations Rate rather than the depo. It does not change the sign of the leg against a 2.65 projection, but a future implementation has to pick A1's rate, not ours.
